tier_reason: First-party suite by Yao's author (yardstiq/quantum-benchmarks: yao/benchmarks.jl, qulacs/benchmarks.py, pyquest/benchmarks.py, bin/plot) with the CPU (Xeon Gold 6230) and Julia 1.3.0 stated, but the C/C++ compilers and flags are not stated (only derivable from the packages' build configs) and results exist only as log-scale chart images, so not A; the headline parameterized-circuit win comes from unequal work, while the same-work single-gate rows show a 1.8-2.5x win only against QuEST built at -O2 through a Python cffi wrapper.

corrections.baseline: Qulacs 0.1.9 (C++ library driven from Python through pybind11, one Python call per gate or circuit) and QuEST via pyquest-cffi 0.1.1 (C library driven from Python through cffi, one Python call per gate), single-thread full-amplitude state-vector simulation
corrections.claimed_speedup: Read off the repo's 'relative to Yao' chart images images/gates_relative.png and images/pcircuit_relative.png (log scale, no tables; ratios approximate; bin/plot uses the minimum time for every package). Parameterized circuit (QCBM) at 25 qubits: qulacs about 1.9x and pyquest-cffi (QuEST) about 8x Yao's time; below about 11 qubits qulacs is faster than Yao (about 0.34x of Yao's time at 4 qubits). This circuit does unequal work: Yao makes 19n state-vector passes (each qubit's rotation chain fused into one 2x2 matrix, 8 mid layers, 9 entanglers) while qulacs and QuEST apply 41n separate gates (9 mid layers, 10 entanglers), a 2.16x pass ratio (derived from the benchmark scripts) that covers the whole qulacs gap. Single gates at 25 qubits (same work, one pass each): pyquest-cffi about 2.4x (X), 1.8x (H) and 2.5x (CNOT) Yao's time but about 0.75x on T (QuEST faster); qulacs about 1.0x on X, CNOT and T and about 0.6x on H (qulacs faster), and qulacs is faster than or equal to Yao on all four gates at most sizes between about 11 and 20 qubits (down to about 0.3x on H).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Julia 1.3.0 (LLVM 6.0.1 ORCJIT, skylake target, run without -O flags so Julia's default -O2), BLAS Intel MKL, Python 3.7.3 (from RESULTS.md). Not stated on the results page, derived from package sources: qulacs 0.1.9 exists on PyPI only as an sdist, built by pip through its CMake Release config (CMake default -O3 -DNDEBUG plus -march=native -mtune=native -mfpmath=both, AVX2 SIMD kernels enabled by default, OpenMP limited to 1 thread by OMP_NUM_THREADS=1); pyquest-cffi 0.1.1 is an sdist that builds QuEST through QuEST's own CMake, which sets -O2 (QuEST v3.2.0 CMakeLists; the exact QuEST version bundled by pyquest-cffi 0.1.1 was not checked). GCC version not stated.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.0k stars and 131 forks (Yao.jl); the benchmark repo, now yardstiq/quantum-benchmarks (old Roger-luo URL redirects), has 129 stars
corrections.workload: Minimum time per gate application for X, H, CNOT and T gates on 4 to 25 qubits, and minimum time for a parameterized QCBM circuit (layers of per-qubit Rx/Rz rotations with ring CNOT entanglers) on 4 to 25 qubits, single thread (OMP/MKL/JULIA threads set to 1), Yao v0.6.1 per RESULTS.md (yao/Manifest.toml at the May 2020 refactor pins Yao 0.6.2 and YaoBlocks 0.10.3) against qulacs, QuEST (pyquest-cffi), qiskit-aer, ProjectQ, Cirq and PennyLane.
corrections.caveats: First-party: the suite is written by Yao's author (reviewed by maintainers of several competitors per its acknowledgements). Results are marked 'only up to date till 2020'; the chart images were last regenerated on 2020-05-29 and the benchmark repo's last commit is 2022-05-17, with old package versions (qulacs 0.1.9, Julia 1.3.0). RESULTS.md and the README give only chart images, so every ratio is read off a log-scale chart. Unequal work in the parameterized circuit: YaoBlocks 0.10.3 PutBlock apply! calls instruct!(r, mat_matchreg(r, content), locs), so Yao's put(i=>chain(Rz, Rx, Rz)) is one dense 2x2 pass per qubit per layer, and Yao's build_circuit(k, 9, ...) has 8 mid layers and 9 entanglers where qulacs/QuEST build_circuit(n, 9, ...) has 9 and 10, giving 19n Yao passes against 41n qulacs/QuEST gate passes (2.16x); the reported 1.9x over qulacs is therefore not a per-gate or language win (qulacs' QuantumCircuitOptimizer gate fusion was not used). Single gates use different target qubits (Yao qubit 2 one-based, qulacs and QuEST qubit 3 zero-based) and Yao starts from rand_state while qulacs/QuEST start from |0>. qulacs and QuEST are timed through Python (pybind11 and cffi), so below about 10 qubits their numbers are dominated by Python call overhead; pyquest-cffi's QCBM function also calls np.random.rand inside the timed region. QuEST is built at -O2 (QuEST's CMake default) rather than -O3; qulacs is built at -O3 -march=native with AVX2 kernels and matches or beats Yao on single gates at large sizes. RESULTS.md's text calls panel d 'Toffolli' but the chart and bin/plot show the T gate; the relative charts label their y axis 'ns' though they plot ratios. The current quest/ directory holds a newer C++ google-benchmark harness (QFT only) that did not produce these charts. The baseline is not a C or C++ program at a stated -O3.
corrections.why_faster: Parameterized circuit: less work in Yao's script, not Julia codegen; Yao fuses each qubit's rotation chain into one 2x2 matrix application and its circuit has one fewer mid layer and entangler, so it makes 19n state passes against 41n for qulacs and QuEST. Single gates: Yao's specialised instruct! kernels (Julia/LLVM, skylake target) beat QuEST's generic C loops built at -O2 and called through pyquest-cffi on X, H and CNOT, but not on T, and show no win at 25 qubits over qulacs' AVX2 kernels built at -O3 -march=native.

notes: Chart readings in the record match images/gates_relative.png and images/pcircuit_relative.png, but the headline 1.9x over qulacs on the parameterized circuit is explained by unequal work (Yao fuses per-qubit rotation chains and runs one fewer layer: 19n vs 41n state passes, verified in yao/benchmarks.jl, qulacs/benchmarks.py, pyquest/benchmarks.py and YaoBlocks 0.10.3 put_block.jl/chain.jl). The only same-work win is 1.8-2.5x on X/H/CNOT against QuEST at -O2 through pyquest-cffi (QuEST faster on T); against qulacs at -O3 -march=native Yao is equal or slower on single gates at 11-25 qubits. Keep at C with these shortcomings; benchmark repo moved to yardstiq/quantum-benchmarks.
